Y: 'Meta removed the old existing-customer budget cap in 2025' is stated as fact without a source (it may be partly true but is not grounded)

reasons: All three budgets add up exactly to ₹10,00,000. I checked the claims I could reach on the live site and found them true: the Chennai/Harrington Road store, exchange at 80% for diamond and 70% for gemstone, PayPal-only international carts of $200 to $3,000 paid DDU, 20+ years, 30,000+ orders, 4.8 Google rating and the 1-on-1 styling session. Product prices and delivery times sit on JS-rendered pages I could not open. Z stands out as the most Gehna-specific and client-ready. Its order-by date table ties real delivery lead times to wedding dates, Karthigai Deepam and Christmas, it keeps lines few, and its kill/scale rules carry honest caveats. X has the most rigorous maths: break-even sensitivity, learning maths, a ladder with checked step-days and well-defined test gates. But it is padded with internal references ('knowledge.md §3.3', 'context/facts.md', 'DECISIONS.md', 'I'm Bianca') that make it unsendable, and it is dense. Y is thorough and rich in products, but it has internal contradictions. Its new-buyer target CPA of ₹12,000 sits above its own break-even (40% × ₹28,000 = ₹11,200). Its forecast counts ~172 'real buyers' from chats yet only ~108 total sales. Its set-up and 15-ad production are scheduled for 9–10 Nov, which is effectively already past.

biggest_flaw.X: Not client-ready. It cites internal working files (knowledge.md, context/facts.md, DECISIONS.md) and an AI persona, and its very conservative 20%-margin break-even rests on bestseller median price, not real AOV.
biggest_flaw.Y: Inconsistent economics: the target cost per purchase is above its own break-even, and the forecast mixes 'real buyer' chats with sales. The budget is also split across six lines (incl. an NRI test with PayPal/duty friction and an unmeasurable reach campaign), which starves learning.
biggest_flaw.Z: The test lane is thin (~₹17.5–20k per concept, promote on 2 purchases), so tests can only screen concepts, which it admits. Tracking set-up is lighter than X's (no EMQ target, no UTM spec).

best_thing.X: Fully reconciled budget with a rule-gated scale ladder and clear break-even/learning maths. Stated test kill/keep thresholds can actually be reached at the planned spend.
best_thing.Y: Very detailed, executable campaign builds with real hero products, sample copy, a production schedule, WhatsApp chat tagging and offline-conversion upload, and an MER profit check.
best_thing.Z: The order-by date table links Gehna's real delivery lead times to specific wedding dates, Karthigai Deepam and Christmas. Every ad names a real piece and price, and the plan leads on natural stones and craft rather than discounts.
